 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Shishir Verma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Smt. Nalini Gurung- Panel Lawyer for the respondent
 Order
This first application under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita has been filed on behalf of the applicants for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.86/2026 registered at police station- Madhav Nagar District Katni for commission of offences punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
3. Learned counsel for the submitted the offence charged against the applicant is punishable with maximum imprisonment of seven years.
Thus, the guidelines of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 would be applicable and it is submitted that this Court may observe the aforesaid guidelines.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, he prays for anticipatory bail.
4.

Learned counsel for the respondent-State submitted that considering the nature of offence, the applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17667 2 MCRC-9941-2026 bail.

5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and the material available on record,
no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

6. So far as issuance of direction in the light of the Arnesh Kumar (supra), it is not incumbent because being a direction issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the investigating agency is expected to follow the same upto the extent applicability thereof in the present case.
